title: Instance settings
description: Settings for this whole installation of Conversa: email, the Meta app, the human check and who may sign up. Only instance admins see this page.
loadFailed: The instance settings did not load

noPermission.title: Only instance admins can change these settings
noPermission.description: Ask the person who set up this installation to make you an instance admin, or to change the setting for you.

mail.title: Email
mail.description: The mail server Conversa sends invitations and password resets through.
mail.off: Email is off. Until you set it up, invitations show a link to copy and people cannot reset a forgotten password themselves.
mail.hostHint: The host name your mail provider gives you for sending.

tls.label: TLS from the start
tls.description: Encrypted from the first byte. Usually port 465.

starttls.label: STARTTLS
starttls.description: Starts plain, then switches to encryption, and refuses servers that cannot. Usually port 587.

none.label: No encryption
none.description: Only for a mail server on the same machine or network, such as a local test server.

mail.usernameHint: Leave empty if the server accepts mail without signing in.
mail.turnOffDialogDescription: The server, sign-in details and sender are forgotten. Invitations will show a link to copy, and password reset by email stops working.

test.hint: Sent to {email} with the saved settings.
test.failedTitle: The test email was not sent

failure.auth: The mail server refused the username or password. Check them and save again.
failure.connection: Conversa could not reach the mail server. Check the server name and port, and that this machine may connect to it.
failure.timeout: The mail server did not answer in time. Check the port and the connection type.
failure.tls: The secure connection failed. Try the other connection type, or check the port.
failure.rejected: The mail server refused the message. Check that the sender address is one it allows.
failure.unknown: The mail server did not accept the message. Check the settings and try again.

instagram.title: Instagram app
instagram.description: Your Meta app, which every Instagram account connected here authorises. Each installation needs its own.
instagram.off: Instagram is not set up yet. Until it is, nobody can connect an Instagram account.
instagram.sandboxDescription: This installation runs the Instagram sandbox, so the Meta app is not used. You can still save it for when the sandbox is turned off.
instagram.appIdHint: Shown under API setup with Instagram login. It is not the App ID at the top of the Meta dashboard, which belongs to Facebook.
instagram.appSecretHint: Shown next to the Instagram app ID. Conversa uses it to check that webhooks really come from Meta.
instagram.verifyTokenHint: Any random text. Paste the same value into the Meta dashboard when you set up webhooks.
instagram.removeDialogDescription: Connected accounts stop receiving comments and messages, and nobody can connect a new one until the app is added again.

tiktok.title: TikTok app
tiktok.description: Your TikTok for Business developer app, which every TikTok account connected here authorises. TikTok accounts answer direct messages only.
tiktok.off: TikTok is not set up yet. Until it is, nobody can connect a TikTok account.
tiktok.sandboxDescription: This installation runs the sandbox, so the TikTok app is not used. You can still save it for when the sandbox is turned off.
tiktok.limitsBody: TikTok cannot message the author of a comment, so only direct messages start automations, and you can only answer people who wrote first. Its messaging API needs TikTok's approval, is not available for accounts registered in the EEA, the UK or Switzerland, and needs an extra review for US accounts. Links are written into the message, because TikTok has no link buttons.
tiktok.invalid: TikTok did not accept the app ID and secret. Copy both again from the app's Basic Information page.

steps.create: In the <portal>TikTok API for Business portal</portal>, create a developer app and upload its logo.
steps.permissions: Under Scope of permission, select TikTok Accounts and Business Messaging, and request messaging access for your accounts.
steps.redirect: Add the redirect URL below as the TikTok account holder redirect URL, exactly as shown, ending in a slash.
steps.paste: Copy the app ID, the secret and the TikTok account holder authorization URL from Basic Information into the fields below.
steps.webhook: Conversa registers the webhook URL with TikTok when the first account connects. It is shown here for reference.

tiktok.appIdHint: The numeric App ID on the app's Basic Information page.
tiktok.appSecretHint: Shown next to the App ID. Conversa uses it to check that webhooks really come from TikTok.
tiktok.authorizationUrlHint: TikTok builds it from the app's permissions. Paste it as it is; Conversa adds what it needs.
tiktok.removeDialogDescription: Connected accounts stop receiving messages, and nobody can connect a new one until the app is added again.

guide.title: Set up your Meta app
guide.intro: Nine steps in Meta's developer dashboard and the Instagram app. It takes about 20 minutes.
guide.menuNote: Menu names are as of 2026. Meta renames them now and then, so look for the closest match.
guide.subscribe: Then turn on Subscribe for these three fields:
guide.verifyTokenHidden: The verify token is shown only until it is saved. To paste it again, click Replace on the webhook verify token field below, generate a new one, save, and paste that.

create.title: Create the app
create.see: A short wizard that asks for an app name, a contact email and a use case.
create.do: Name the app (for example “Conversa”), choose the use case “Manage messaging & content on Instagram”, and choose Business if it asks for an app type. You can skip connecting a business portfolio.

credentials.title: Copy the Instagram app ID and secret
credentials.where: Your app › Use cases › Manage messaging & content on Instagram › Customize › API setup with Instagram login
credentials.see: A box with the Instagram app name, the Instagram app ID and the Instagram app secret (click Show to see it).
credentials.do: Paste the Instagram app ID and the Instagram app secret into the form below. Click Generate token for the webhook verify token, then save.
credentials.mistake: The Instagram app ID is not the App ID at the top of the dashboard or under App settings › Basic: that one is the Facebook app ID. Using it makes connecting fail with “Invalid redirect_uri” or “Invalid platform app”.

webhooks.title: Connect the webhooks
webhooks.where: API setup with Instagram login › Configure webhooks
webhooks.see: A Callback URL field, a Verify token field and a Verify and save button, then a list of webhook fields.
webhooks.do: Paste both values and click Verify and save.
webhooks.mistake: Save the form in Conversa before you click Verify and save. Meta calls Conversa right away with the token, and the check fails if Conversa does not have it yet.

login.title: Set up Instagram business login
login.where: API setup with Instagram login › Set up Instagram business login › Business login settings
login.see: A panel with OAuth redirect URIs, a Deauthorize callback URL and a Data deletion request URL.
login.do: Paste the three addresses and save.
login.mistake: The redirect URI goes here, in Instagram's Business login settings, not under Facebook Login › Settings › Valid OAuth Redirect URIs. Instagram ignores that list and answers “Invalid redirect_uri”.

basic.title: Fill in the basic settings
basic.see: The app's display name, contact email, legal links, icon and category.
basic.do: Paste the privacy policy and terms addresses. Under User data deletion, choose Data deletion callback URL and paste that address. Choose a category, upload an app icon and save changes.
basic.mistake: The app icon must be 1024 × 1024 pixels. Without the icon, the privacy policy and the terms, Meta will not let you switch the app to Live in step 8.

roles.title: Add your Instagram account as a tester
roles.where: App roles › Roles › Add people › Instagram Tester
roles.see: A dialog that asks for an Instagram username.
roles.do: Add each Instagram account you will connect. Then, signed in to Instagram as that account, open the Tester invites tab in Apps and websites and accept the invite.
roles.mistake: An account that is not an accepted Instagram Tester fails to connect with “Insufficient developer role”. The invite counts only once it is accepted on Instagram.

account.title: Prepare the Instagram account
account.see: The account type and the message settings of the account.
account.do: Make it a professional account (Business or Creator) under Account type and tools. Then open Messages and story replies › Connected tools and turn on Allow access to messages.
account.mistake: With Allow access to messages off, direct messages never reach Conversa and private replies cannot be sent, even when comments arrive.

publish.title: Switch the app to Live
publish.where: Publish, in the left menu (or the App mode switch at the top of the dashboard)
publish.see: A checklist of what Meta still needs before the app can go Live.
publish.do: Fix anything the checklist marks, usually the icon, privacy policy or terms from step 5, then publish until App mode shows Live.
publish.mistake: While the app is in Development mode, Meta does not send real webhooks. Verify and save works, but comments and messages never reach Conversa.
publish.note: Live with standard access is enough for accounts that have a role on the app. To connect other people's accounts, the app needs advanced access through App Review: see docs/instagram.md.

connect.title: Connect the account in Conversa
connect.see: Your connected accounts and a Connect Instagram account button.
connect.do: Click Connect Instagram account, sign in as the tester account and allow the permissions. Then comment on one of its posts from another account: the connection status should show an event within a minute.

status.title: Connection status
status.loadFailed: The connection status did not load. Nothing was changed.
status.sandbox: Instagram is simulated on this installation, so there is no Meta app to check.
status.credentialsHow: Meta has no direct check for Instagram login apps. Conversa asks Meta to exchange a sign-in code that cannot work and reads why it was refused, so this is a good sign, not a guarantee.

invalid.title: Meta did not accept the app ID or secret
invalid.body: Check that you copied the Instagram app ID and secret from API setup with Instagram login, not the Facebook app ID at the top of the dashboard.

hints.unknown: Meta answered in a way Conversa does not recognise, or could not be reached. Check again in a minute.

notVerified.title: Meta has not verified the webhook yet
notVerified.body: Save the Instagram app in Conversa first, then click Verify and save in Meta's Configure webhooks.

quiet.title: No events from Instagram yet
quiet.body: Meta verified the webhook but has not sent anything since. Is your Meta app in Live mode? Is Allow access to messages on in the Instagram app?

turnstile.title: Human check
turnstile.description: Cloudflare Turnstile on sign-up, sign-in and password reset, to keep bots out.
turnstile.optional: Optional. Without it, sign-in is still protected by rate limits and account lockout.
turnstile.on: Turnstile is on. Sign-up, sign-in and password reset ask for the check.
turnstile.siteKeyHint: From the Turnstile widget you create for this site in the Cloudflare dashboard.
turnstile.turnOffDialogDescription: Sign-up, sign-in and password reset stop asking for it. The keys are forgotten.

signup.title: Sign-up
signup.description: Who may create an account on this installation.
signup.label: Who can sign up
signup.inviteOnlyDescription: People join when a workspace admin invites them.
signup.openDescription: Anyone who can open this address can create an account and their own workspace.

saved.invite_only: Sign-up is now by invitation only
saved.open: Sign-up is now open to anyone

admins.title: Instance admins
admins.description: Instance admins change these settings. Workspace roles are separate: an instance admin sees only the workspaces they belong to.
admins.label: People on this installation
admins.name: Name
admins.loadFailed: The list of people did not load
admins.revoked: {name} is no longer an instance admin
admins.revokeDialogDescription: {name} keeps their account and workspaces, but can no longer change the instance settings.
admins.revokeSelfDialogDescription: You keep your account and workspaces, but you will no longer see this page. Another instance admin can give the access back.

setup.title: Set up this installation
setup.description: A few things Conversa needs to work fully. Skip any of them and come back later from Instance settings.
setup.label: Steps to set up the installation
setup.sandboxDescription: This installation runs the Instagram sandbox, so you can skip this step and try Conversa without a Meta app.
setup.turnstileOptional: Optional. Add it if this installation is reachable from the internet and you want to keep bots away from sign-in.

instagram.title: Instagram app
instagram.description: Connects your Meta app, so your team can connect Instagram accounts.

turnstile.description: Adds Cloudflare Turnstile to sign-up and sign-in.

version.title: Version

mismatch.description: The web app runs v{web} and the API runs v{api}. Update both images to the same release and restart them.
